Project: Django. Upgrade being assessed: 3.2 -> 4.2. This change was introduced in release 4.1. Source: Django 4.1 release notes (official_release_notes). Section: Django 4.1 release notes / What's new in Django 4.1 / Minor features / Forms. Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): [ { "release": "4.1", "field": "python", "value": ">=3.8", "source_id": "dj_pypi@4.1", "json_path": "info.requires_python" } ] ITEM: <<< The default template used to render forms when cast to a string, e.g. in templates as {{ form }}, is now configurable at the project-level by setting form_template_name on the class provided for FORM_RENDERER. Form.template_name is now a property deferring to the renderer, but may be overridden with a string value to specify the template name per-form class. Similarly, the default template used to render formsets can be specified via the matching formset_template_name renderer attribute. >>> PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only): <<< Django 4.1 release notes / What's new in Django 4.1 / Minor features / Forms: The default template used to render forms when cast to a string, e.g. in templates as {{ form }}, is now configurable at the project-level by setting form_template_name on the class provided for FORM_RENDERER. Form.template_name is now a property deferring to the renderer, but may be overridden with a string value to specify the template name per-form class. Similarly, the default template used to render formsets can be specified via the matching formset_template_name renderer attribute. The new div.html form template, referencing Form.template_name_div attribute, and matching Form.as_div method, render forms using HTML
elements. This new output style is recommended over the existing as_table, as_p and as_ul styles, as the template implements
and to group related inputs and is easier for screen reader users to navigate. The div-based output will become the default rendering style from Django 5.0. In order to smooth adoption of the new
output style, two transitional form renderer classes are available: django.forms.renderers.DjangoDivFormRenderer and django.forms.renderers.Jinja2DivFormRenderer, for the Django and Jinja2 template backends respectively. You can apply one of these via the FORM_RENDERER setting. For example: FORM_RENDERER = "django.forms.renderers.DjangoDivFormRenderer" Once the
output style is the default, from Django 5.0, these transitional renderers will be deprecated, for removal in Django 6.0. The FORM_RENDERER declaration can be removed at that time. If the new
output style is not appropriate for your project, you should define a renderer subclass specifying form_template_name and formset_template_name for your required style, and set FORM_RENDERER accordingly. For example, for the

output style used by as_p, you would define a form renderer setting form_template_name to "django/forms/p.html" and formset_template_name to "django/forms/formsets/p.html". The new legend_tag allows rendering field labels in tags via the new tag argument of label_tag. The new edit_only argument for modelformset_factory and inlineformset_factory allows preventing new objects creation. The js and css class attributes of Media now allow using hashable objects, not only path strings, as long as those objects implement the html() method (typically when decorated with the html_safe decorator). Give the reason. For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules: 1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting. 2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 4.1 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply. 3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected. 4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain". 5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string. 6. Empty list if no literal symbol. 8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved. 9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only. 10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later). 11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null. response.context_reason: This is an additive feature. The default form template can now be set per project via form_template_name on the FORM_RENDERER class, and formsets get a matching formset_template_name attribute. Form.template_name is now a property deferring to the renderer, but the text says it may still be overridden with a string per form class. The text states no required action at 4.2. The div-based output only becomes the default from Django 5.0, and the transitional renderers are opt-in.
